module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 848

Is the maximum size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never
squarefree (for all $a, b \in A$) achieved by taking those $n \equiv 7 \pmod{25}$?

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/848](https://www.erdosproblems.com/848)
 - [Er92b] Erdős, P. "Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics,
   and geometry." Resenhas do Instituto de Matemático e Estatística da Universidade
   de São Paulo 2.2 (1995): 165-186.
 - [Sa25] Sawhney, M. "Problem 848." (2025)
   https://www.math.columbia.edu/~msawhney/Problem_848.pdf
 - Full formal proof of asymptotic result: https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos848

/-- A set $A$ has the non-squarefree product property if $ab + 1$ is not squarefree
for all $a, b ∈ A$. -/
def NonSquarefreeProductProp (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ¬Squarefree (a * b + 1)

/-- The candidate extremal set: $\{n ∈ \{0, \dots, N-1\} : n ≡ 7 (mod 25)\}$. -/
def A₇ (N : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range N).filter (fun n => n % 25 = 7)

/-- The Erdős Problem 848 statement for a fixed $N$: any set $A ⊆ \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ with
the non-squarefree product property has cardinality at most $|A₇(N)|$. -/
def Erdos848For (N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.range N → NonSquarefreeProductProp A →
    A.card ≤ (A₇ N).card

/-- Is the maximum size of a set $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that $ab + 1$ is never squarefree
(for all $a, b ∈ A$) achieved by taking those $n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}$?

This asks whether `Erdos848 N` holds for all $N$ (formulated using `A ⊆ Finset.range N`).

This was solved for all sufficiently large $N$ by Sawhney in this note. In fact, Sawhney proves
something slightly stronger, that there exists some constant $c>0$ such that if
$\lvert A\rvert \geq (\frac{1}{25}-c)N$ and $N$ is large then $A$ is contained in either
$\{ n\equiv 7\pmod{25}\}$ or $\{n\equiv 18\pmod{25}\}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_848 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ N, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

/-- There exists $N₀$ such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $A ⊆ \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfies that $ab + 1$
is never squarefree for all $a, b ∈ A$, then $|A| ≤ |\{n ≤ N : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}|$.

More precisely, Sawhney proves: there exist absolute constants $η > 0$ and $N₀$
such that for all $N ≥ N₀$, if $|A| ≥ (1/25 - η)N$ then $A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 7 \pmod{25}\}$ or
$A ⊆ \{n : n ≡ 18 \pmod{25}\}$.

A complete formal Lean 4 proof is available at:
https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/The-Obstacle-Is-The-Way/erdos-banger/blob/1cc2ac8e9d70516e979733c6ea5c4d2eb652d1f5/formal/lean/Erdos/848.lean"]
theorem erdos_848.variants.asymptotic : ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, Erdos848For N := by
  sorry

end Erdos848

findings.description: The bibliography entry labelled [Er92b] gives the title, journal, year, and pages of a different paper: the 1995 Resenhas survey. The source containing this question is Erdős's 1992 paper 'Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics', Problem 23 on p. 239. This reference error does not affect the Lean mathematics.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, Le Matematiche 47(2) (1992), pp. 231–240, Problem 23, says: 'Assume next that a_i a_j + 1 is never squarefree. This is satisfied if a_i ≡ 7 (mod 25). Is this sequence maximal?' See https://lematematiche.dmi.unict.it/index.php/lematematiche/article/download/587/555. Sawhney's cited note also identifies this 1992 paper as reference [2]. The separately inspected Resenhas paper is https://www.revistas.usp.br/resenhasimeusp/article/download/74798/78366.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Er92b] bibliography entry with: Erdős, Paul, 'Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics', Le Matematiche 47(2) (1992), 231–240, Problem 23, p. 239.

status_issues.source_status: The all-N problem remains open, classified as 'decidable' (reduced to a finite computation). Sawhney's 2025 result proves the bound only for sufficiently large N.
status_issues.evidence: The current teorth/erdosproblems data/problems.yaml entry 848 records informal_status.state = 'decidable', last_update = '2025-10-19'; its README explains that 'decidable' problems remain open but have been reduced to a finite computation. Sawhney's Proposition 1.1 begins 'There exists an integer N₀ such that if N ≥ N₀ then the following holds.' The exact linked formal-proof file explicitly distinguishes 'Original Problem 848 (STILL OPEN)' for ALL N from its theorem problem_848_asymptotic.

reformulations.difference: The mathematical right-hand side uses sets in Finset.range N and a universal cardinality upper bound, rather than stating that the residue-7 candidate attains the maximum in {1,…,N}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An admissible set cannot contain 0, since 0·0+1=1 is squarefree. Consequently, for every M, Erdos848For (M+1) is exactly the source's bound on {1,…,M}, with the candidate sets equal; Erdos848For 0 is true. Thus the universally quantified problems are equivalent. Also, any two elements congruent to 7 modulo 25 have their product plus one divisible by 25, so the candidate is admissible and the upper bound says it attains the maximum. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the file's sorry-backed theorems. The answer/status record is addressed separately.

reformulations.difference: The variant expresses Sawhney's existential-threshold result using eventual truth at Filter.atTop and the half-open interval Finset.range N.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, eventual truth at atTop is equivalent to existence of N₀ such that the predicate holds for every N≥N₀. Excluding 0 from admissible sets identifies Erdos848For (M+1) with the source's bound on {1,…,M}; shifting the threshold preserves eventual truth. The exact equivalence with an explicit threshold statement on Finset.Icc 1 N was proved in scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. All three definitions and both theorem statements were checked. Scratch proofs establish zero exclusion, candidate admissibility, the N≤7 cases, and the stated reformulations; their printed axiom lists contain no sorryAx. An independent exhaustive maximum-clique computation found no counterexample for N≤2000. The live erdosproblems.com pages were Cloudflare-blocked despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the original papers and the current community database were used instead. The linked external theorem has exactly the required asymptotic statement and no active sorry/custom-axiom declarations were found in its source.
